en.title: Global Macro — Risk assets resist the bond selloff as stress concentrates in rates and emerging-market FX
en.deck: Global equities are heading for their best week since early August even as long sovereign yields remain near multi-decade highs, revealing a selective cross-asset shock rather than uniform tightening.
en.regime: Cross-asset divergence: equity risk appetite remains resilient while long sovereign yields and selected emerging-market currencies absorb more of the rate-and-energy shock.
en.key_risk: If energy de-escalation fails or long yields stay above 5%, equity resilience could converge downward toward the stress already visible in duration and selected emerging-market FX.

pt-BR.title: Global Macro — Ativos de risco resistem à venda de títulos enquanto a pressão se concentra em juros e câmbio emergente
pt-BR.deck: As bolsas globais caminham para sua melhor semana desde o início de agosto mesmo com juros soberanos longos perto de máximas de várias décadas, revelando um choque seletivo entre ativos em vez de aperto uniforme.
pt-BR.regime: Divergência entre ativos: o apetite por risco em ações permanece resiliente enquanto juros soberanos longos e algumas moedas emergentes absorvem parcela maior do choque de juros e energia.
pt-BR.key_risk: Se o alívio energético fracassar ou os juros longos permanecerem acima de 5%, a resiliência das ações pode convergir para baixo em direção ao estresse já visível em duração e alguns câmbios emergentes.

novelty_gate.dominant_delta: The new 25 September signal is the cross-asset divergence itself: global equities were heading for their best week since early August even as U.S. and Japanese long yields remained near multi-decade highs, while the Indonesian rupiah was heading for its worst week since late May.
novelty_gate.repetition_control: Long yields are treated as inherited background from the 22-24 September editions. The report leads with selective absorption across equities, duration and emerging-market FX, and explicitly rejects the prior draft's unsupported claim that a broad refinancing squeeze is already observed.

revision_reason: QA rework after revision 1 rejection: localized remaining PT-BR financial anglicisms and removed an unsupported sanctions-economic-coercion taxonomy classification. The cross-asset divergence thesis, factual claims, EN source and visual evidence remain unchanged.
qa_fixes_applied: Reframed long yields from the lead thesis to background evidence and made the 25 September equity-versus-bond divergence the dominant new mechanism.
Removed claims that broad sovereign or corporate refinancing stress is already observed; retained mortgage pricing as observed evidence and labeled wider refinancing effects as conditional.
Added contrary evidence from the resilience of global equities and dispersion across Asian currencies.
Preserved EN/PT-BR semantic and visual parity with one analytical table, one Treasury chart and one transmission flow in each locale.
Localized remaining PT-BR financial terminology: valuation → precificação/avaliações de ativos; intraday → durante a sessão; first capex occurrence → investimento de capital (capex).
Removed sanctions-economic-coercion from phenomena because sanctions/economic coercion are not materially analyzed in this edition.
Preserved the approved novelty direction: cross-asset divergence remains the lead thesis; no broad refinancing-stress claim was reintroduced.
Corrected rejection provenance: supersedes_rejected_commit now references the QA rejection commit 29b7f54e4a302f18388b70e3573b6af823fbf8b4.
